name: Question Tags
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Question Tags module! This is the art of asking for confirmation. In French, you can just say 'N'est-ce pas?' or 'Non?' at the end of any sentence. In English, this is impossible. We have a complex system where the end of the sentence must mathematically match the beginning.
contrastiveExplanation:
The Mirror Rule:
English: You must repeat the Auxiliary Verb and the Subject Pronoun. (She is -> Isn't she?).
French: Uses a fixed phrase (N'est-ce pas?).

Polarity Switch:
English: Positive Sentence -> Negative Tag. Negative Sentence -> Positive Tag.
French: Usually adds a negative tag (non?).

The 'Do' Rescue:
English: If there is no auxiliary (Simple Tenses), use Do/Does/Did.
French: No change in structure.

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Direct translation of 'N'est-ce pas'. The tag must match the subject 'You'.

commonErrors.wrong: You like rice, like you not?
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Trying to use the main verb in the tag. Use 'Do/Does'.
